subject: Post-demo: Zenlyte performance pack and Redwood-verified profiles
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alice Morgan <alice@zenlyte.com>; Rajesh Iyer <rajesh.iyer@zenlyte.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-14T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Zenlyte performance pack and Redwood-verified profiles

Hi Alice / Rajesh —

Great to connect today. Quick recap and the artifacts we promised: attached is a compact performance pack with Redwood-verified profiles for the three candidate models we discussed plus raw benchmark links and our sample prompt set. Key highlights: 

- Recommended models (based on your convo today: retrieval-heavy NLU and short-form generation):
  - open-redwood-7B-fp16: best latency per cost for conversational latency targets under 150ms p95 for 128-token responses.
  - open-redwood-13B-q4: balanced quality and throughput; p95 220ms at 32 TPS with continuous batching (see profile).
  - open-rlhf-70B-q8: highest quality, used for critical reranking and hallucination-sensitive tasks; higher latency (p95 ~420ms) and cost.

- Benchmarks & perf summary included: throughput (TPS) at 8/32/128 concurrency points, p50/p95 latencies, and token-cost estimates. The attached redwood_profiles_20260914.csv has the per-model lines used in the demo.

- Quality/regression notes: we observed a small regression on factual recall when moving from fp16 -> aggressive q4_0 quantization on the 13B in our internal eval on your prompt set (sample attached). For your use-case (entity extraction + short summary), we recommend running an additional focused eval for hallucination-prone prompts before committing to q4_0 rollouts.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Marcus to run a focused hallucination/regression sweep on your sample prompt set (we'll use the exact prompts you shared).
2) If results look good, we spin up a 2-week trial on Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) to validate latency SLOs under your traffic shape.
3) Sales/legal can pull together a mutual action plan + trial terms (I linked a starter MA below).

Attachments: zenlyte_benchmark_report.pdf (summary), redwood_profiles_20260914.csv (per-model metrics), sample_prompt_set.txt

If this layout looks good I can schedule Marcus for the eval tomorrow afternoon PST. Preferred time?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0129

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Zenlyte performance pack and Redwood-verified profiles

Thanks Hannah — I'll pick this up. Quick technical notes so Alice and Rajesh know what I'll run: 

- Test plan: 1) hallucination/regression sweep using your sample_prompt_set.txt across the three recommended variants; 2) concurrency sweep at 8/32/128 to reproduce the TPS/latency rows in the CSV; 3) KV-cache warm/cold tests for your retrieval flows.
- Configs I'll use: dynamic batching cap = 128 tokens, kernel profile = aten-fast for fp16 paths, fallback q8 kernels for 70B. I'll attach the small script I'll run (perf_commands.sh).
- Quick recommendation: if cost is a hard constraint, start with open-redwood-7B-fp16 + a lightweight reranker (13B-q4) for the tight-latency endpoints; keep the 70B for nightly reranks. That gives the best mix of throughput and hallucination control.

I'll run the sweep today around 2pm PST and post results to the Drive folder. If you want the Dedicated trial we can pre-provision a 2-GPU pool to mirror your expected peak.

-marcus
Marcus Lin

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Zenlyte performance pack and Redwood-verified profiles

Hannah / Marcus — thanks for the follow-up and for the pack. A few clarifying points from our side: 

- Our priority is minimizing hallucinations on user-facing summaries while keeping interactive latency below ~250ms p95 for 95% of traffic. We expect ~40k MAUs and bursts up to ~90 RPS.
- The regression you flagged for q4_0 is exactly the risk we need to validate — happy to have Marcus run the targeted sweep on our prompts. Please include the prompt variants that include ambiguous entity references (we've seen the biggest failures there).
- Can you share estimated monthly unit pricing for the three configuration patterns (7B fp16 baseline, 13B q4 baseline, mixed 7B+13B with nightly 70B reranker)? An order-of-magnitude comparison will help us decide trial sizing.

Also, could you call out the p95 numbers for cold cache vs warmed KV-cache for the 13B-q4 variant? That's important for our initial load spikes.

If possible let's schedule the 30-min technical spike on Thu 9/17 10am PT. Does that work?

Thanks,
Alice Morgan
VP Product | Zenlyte
alice@zenlyte.com

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Zenlyte performance pack and Redwood-verified profiles

Alice — perfect, thanks for the clear priorities. Confirming next steps and answers inline: 

1) Marcus will run the hallucination/regression sweep against the ambiguous-entity variants in sample_prompt_set.txt tomorrow (results + per-prompt failure rates in CSV).
2) Cold vs warm KV-cache: for 13B-q4 we typically see ~1.8x p95 improvement when KV-cache is warm; I'll include explicit cold/warm rows in Marcus's output.
3) Pricing: I attached a short pricing sketch in the Drive link. High-level monthly estimates (order-of-magnitude):
   - 7B fp16 baseline: ~$4k–$7k for your expected baseline traffic (MAU & RPS mix).
   - 13B q4 baseline: ~$9k–$14k depending on concurrency profiles.
   - Mixed (7B + 13B + nightly 70B reranker): ~$12k–$20k.

4) Technical spike: Thu 2026-09-17 10:00am PT works for Marcus and me — booking now. I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda: 1) run a short live query set, 2) review the sweep results, 3) discuss Dedicated trial sizing and next steps for the MA.

5) I've attached redwood_profiles_20260914.csv again and pushed the benchmark PDF to Drive. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Zny-zenlyte-bench

If that all looks good I'll move the trial MA into HubSpot and loop in sales ops for trial provisioning.

Best,
Hannah
